gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI AC180's ECO mode can switch off the 12 V DC output when the load stays below a 5–10 W threshold for 1–4 hours. A compressor cooler holding a few insulin pens in a cool room averages about 9–11 W and sits near zero between compressor cycles, so the published runtime holds only if DC ECO is turned off.
standout_why: I compared willitrunpower.com (cited), our own dealectric.com page (cited) and the first results of the live search. Willrun only says 'some stations switch off idle ports after a timeout', with no threshold, duration or model. Our page doesn't mention ECO or DC auto-off at all. GOES and SCHSA are general health advice with no station specs. Willrun already has the 15 W AC self-consumption and Dometic's 0.92 Ah/h and 6.5 A figures, so those aren't new. The ECO thresholds are new, and so is the gap between Dometic's annual rating and its hot-room rating.
decides: It keeps the AC180 plus a 12 V compressor cooler as the pick, but it attaches a setup step the pick depends on. Turn off DC ECO (Setting mode: hold AC+DC for about 2 s with the AC output off), or the 2-day runtime math doesn't apply. It also supports the DC-only setup with a number: the manual's roughly 15 W self-consumption over 48 h is about 720 Wh, which is most of the AC180's roughly 980 Wh usable. A mini-fridge on the AC outlet won't last two days on this unit.

findings.label: ECO mode auto-off thresholds (AC and DC set separately)
findings.value: DC: 5–10 W threshold; AC: 15–30 W threshold; off after 1, 2, 3 or 4 h below threshold
findings.source_title: Bluetti AC180 Portable Power Station Manual (ManualsLib)
findings.note: Manual text: 'When operating on ECO mode, the AC/DC output will automatically turn off if the AC180 is bearing low or no load for a while.' Enter Setting mode by holding AC+DC for about 2 s with the screen on and AC off. Setting mode exits after 1 min without saving. The manual doesn't say whether ECO is on at the factory. The 9–11 W cooler average uses Dometic's 0.92 Ah/h × 12 V = 11 W hot-room figure, quoted by Willrun; a cooler room lowers it.

findings.label: Self-consumption (inverter on)
findings.value: about 15 W, which is about 720 Wh over 48 h
findings.source_title: Bluetti AC180 Portable Power Station Manual (ManualsLib)
findings.note: Manual: 'The self-consumption of AC180 is about 15W.' 15 W × 48 h = 720 Wh, against about 980 Wh usable (1,152 Wh × 0.85). This is why the cooler has to run from the 12 V port.

findings.label: 12 V car outlet rating
findings.source_title: Bluetti AC180 Portable Power Station Manual (ManualsLib)
findings.note: Covers the CFX3 25's 6.5 A rated current with headroom.

findings.label: Discharge temperature range
findings.value: -20 to 40 °C (-4 to 104 °F); output limited to 1,500 W between 30 and 40 °C
findings.source_title: Bluetti AC180 Portable Power Station Manual (ManualsLib)
findings.note: Relevant to a summer outage with no air conditioning.

findings.label: Rated current vs annual energy rating (two bases in one manual)
findings.value: 12 V rated current 6.5 A (about 78 W while the compressor runs); annual energy 78 kWh/yr, about 214 Wh/day
findings.source_title: Dometic CFX3 operating manual, technical data, p. 39 (ManualsLib)
findings.note: 78 kWh ÷ 365 = 214 Wh/day, about 8.9 W average. The manual gives no test conditions for the annual figure. Willrun and our page use Dometic's hot-room 0.92 Ah/h (90 °F ambient, 39 °F inside), which is 265 Wh/day. Rated current is the running peak, not the average; using 78 W would overstate daily use about 7×.

findings.label: Maker's stated draw (ECO mode)
findings.value: under 36 W with energy-saving mode on; $169.99 (black, 'for travel' listing) / $144.99 (another 23 qt listing)
findings.source_title: BougeRV 12V 23 Quart Colorful Purple Portable Fridge (BougeRV store search via storecheck)
findings.note: The maker gives a running-draw ceiling, not a daily average, so it can't be compared directly with Dometic's Ah/h or kWh/yr. Prices are from the storecheck search of bougerv.com on 2026-11-13: https://www.bougerv.com/products/12v-23-quart-portable-fridge-black-for-travel at $169.99 and https://www.bougerv.com/products/12v-23-quart-portable-refrigerator-for-travel at $144.99.
